newsitem.title: USA: Alleged U.S. killer seen embarrassed by TV tape.
newsitem.headline: Alleged U.S. killer seen embarrassed by TV tape.

text.p: Jonathan Schmitz buried his face in his hands in embarrassment when a TV talk show played a tape of a man saying he had a secret fantasy for him, according to testimony in Schmitz' murder trial Thursday.

Schmitz, 26, of Lake Orion, a northern suburb of Detroit, is charged with first-degree murder in the death of Scott Amedure, 32, of Orion Township. The two had appeared with a mutual friend, Donna Riley, on a segment of the Jenny Jones daytime talk show on secret admirers with same-sex crushes.

Schmitz says he is heterosexual and the humiliation of the show, combined with mental illnesses from which he suffers, contributed to his killing Amedure with two shotgun blasts to the chest three days after the taping of the show.
Riley told Oakland County Circuit Court jurors Schmitz buried his face in his hands in embarrassment when the show played a previously recorded segment about Amedure's fantasy.
"Jonathan said something to the effect of 'I'm flattered, but I'm a heterosexual,'" Riley said, adding that the audience clapped at that point. The show was taped March 6, 1995, but was never aired.

Under questioning from Assistant Oakland County Prosecutor Roman Kalytiak, Riley said Amedure was never aggressive toward Schmitz and never tried to pressure him sexually. She said the two men had talked previously at her apartment about Amedure's homosexuality and whether Amedure's parents knew he was gay.
"They were joking about it. Jonathan was asking a lot of questions," she said, adding that he seemed very inquisitive about the topic.

Riley said Schmitz had asked if Amedure would be able to help Schmitz select and install ceiling fans in his dining room and bedroom on Sunday, March 12. The testimony could be important because Schmitz's father and lawyers have said Amedure stalked Schmitz despite attempts to stop his advances.

The jury will have the option of convicting Schmitz of first-degree or second-degree murder, manslaughter or reckless discharge causing death. The first-degree murder charge carries a penalty of life imprisonment without parole.
